explanation: The strong Diophantine quintuple conjecture: every Diophantine triple {a, b, c} has at most one extension by d > max(a, b, c), namely the regular one. Because 0 is allowed in the definition, the triple {0, 1, 3} is "Diophantine" (products plus one: 1, 1, 4). It has two extensions with d > 3: d = 8 and d = 120, since d + 1 and 3d + 1 are both squares. Hence HasUniqueExtensionOfForall is false as formalized and the open conjecture is trivially disproved. Excluding 0 from the definition repairs it.
